Nanchang/Changbei Airport
(KHN/ZSCN)
Updated on 2025.10.28
Responsibility Division: First Division
I. Typical unsafe event
None
II. Core Threats
1. Command characteristics: Radar guidance is
commonly used, and direct flight command during the
approach phase may result in a high profile. This is
particularly evident for the blind landing of Flight 03,
which entered from the north.
2. Topography: The southwestern side of the airport
features elevated terrain with a maximum elevation of 841
meters. For the westward approach, the No.03 blind
landing is restricted by the terrain, with the IAF point
strictly limited to 1800 meters (5900 feet). The CN104 is
strictly limited to 1500 meters (4900 feet), and the
Minimum Surveillance and Guidance Altitude (MSGA)
chart can be referenced.
3. Meteorological characteristics: Frequent thunderstorms
in summer with a high likelihood of wind shear
4. Other threats:
(1) The area around this airport is surrounded by
numerous military airfields, with frequent activities of both
military and civilian aircraft. All aircraft entering or leaving

Shanghai/Pudong Airport (PVG/ZSPD)
Updated on January 20,2026
Responsibility Division: Sixth Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Re-flight was caused by loss of visual reference due to
low altitude.
2. The damage of the radar dome was beyond the
standard due to the low altitude bird strike.
II. Core Threats
1. Command characteristics: The apron sometimes
issues push-off start commands, and other times
push-off arrival reports.
2. Runway characteristics: Aircraft typically should not
exceed 50 seconds on the runway after landing. If this cannot
be achieved, the aircraft must notify the controller no later
than 5 minutes before landing.
3. Meteorological characteristics: Low visibility and low
cloud cover are common during winter operations.
4. Other threats:
(1) The investigation found that the activity of
wild ducks and geese in the coastal area of Pudong
Airport is relatively frequent, and the flight altitude of
some birds overlaps with the altitude of aircraft
take-off and landing channels, resulting in a high risk
of bird strikes.

(5) Detailed Description of Typical Safety Incidents:
1. On January 31,2024, an A320 aircraft was operating a
Lanzhou-Shanghai Pudong flight. During a Category 1 blind
landing approach at Pudong Airport's 35L runway, the captain
(PF) and co-pilot (PM) were using the DA (Direct Approach)
system with visible approach lights. When the aircraft
approached 100 feet, there were no visual references except
for the approach lights. The captain decided to return to the
runway, maintaining a radio altitude of 59 feet and
accelerating to TOGA (Takeoff Off-Ground Approach).
During the return, the minimum radio altitude was 35 feet.
The aircraft then diverted to land at Hongqiao Airport, with
6.39 tons of fuel remaining after landing.
2. On December 19,2023, an A321 aircraft operating the
Changchun-Pudong route encountered an ILS approach with
radar guidance on runway 35L at Pudong Airport. During the
high-altitude flight at 600 meters with autopilot engaged, the
aircraft triggered two "TERRAIN" warnings that subsequently
disappeared. After confirming normal instrument readings and
status, the crew continued the approach while maintaining
monitoring and successfully landed at Pudong Airport. Data
analysis indicated the GPWS warning was triggered by
significant changes in the radio altimeter (RA) readings during
the flight. QAR decoding: GMT17:43:31 – Barometer
altimeter 2003 feet, radio altimeter 1916 feet; GMT17:43:32

3. On October 1, 2023, an A320NEO aircraft
operated a flight from Phuket to Shanghai Pudong,
taking off at 23:54 and landing at 04:34 the next day.
Post-landing inspection revealed bird strike marks
(bloodstains and feathers) on the radar dome. Further
examination after the strike identified layered damage
inside the radar dome, which was assessed as
exceeding safety standards. The maximum diameter of
the damaged area measured 370mm. According to
Manual AMM53-15-11-200-001-A01, the damage was
confirmed to exceed safety thresholds. The damaged
radar dome was replaced using Manual
AMM53-15-11-000/400-001-A, with subsequent tests
showing no adverse effects. The crew reported a bird
strike at 500 feet altitude during the approach phase on
Pudong 35L runway. The bird strike confirmation form
was signed by both the airline maintenance department
and the crew. Samples of the bird strike residue were
sent to the Key Laboratory of Bird Strike Residue
Identification at Nanjing Normal University for testing
(Sample ID: ZSPD2023-504). Identification confirmed
the species involved as a green heron (Butorides
striata).

Xiamen/Gaoqi Airport (XMN/ZSAM)
Updated on January 28,2026
Responsibility Division: First Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. There was an incident where the aircraft touched down
with its tail rubbing against the ground due to rainfall and
unstable wind direction during a night flight.
II. Core Threats
1. Command Characteristics:
(1) Strict compliance with altitude, speed, and turning radius
restrictions is required for port entry and departure.
(2) Thunderstorm is restricted in space-time domain.
2. Track surface characteristics: The terrain is higher at Runway
05 and lower at Runway 23.
3. Terrain: The airport is situated at a higher elevation with
complex topography. Its northeastern end borders the sea at a
lower elevation, while the southwestern end adjoins Xiamen Port.
Numerous tall artificial structures in the area significantly impact
takeoff and landing operations.

Kinmen Island, which is relatively close to this airport and requires
strict adherence to flight restrictions specified in the airworthiness
chart. There have been frequent GPS signal interference incidents
near Xiamen Airport, with other airlines repeatedly issuing GPWS
warnings due to GPS signal interference.
(2) In exceptional circumstances, any deviation towards the
coast is strictly prohibited. Pilots must strictly follow ground
instructions to avoid entering airspace over islands such as the
Greater and Lesser Kinmen Islands. For Runway 23, ATC may
designate departure points. Strict adherence to speed limits is
mandatory, and the flight plan explicitly prohibits eastward
deviations, with non-compliance subject to penalties.

NARITAAirport (NRT/RJAA)
Updated on January 26,2026
Responsibility Division: Fifth Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Due to the maritime climate, this airport is prone to wind
shear. The crew should be alert to this risk.
2. Due to frequent flights, this airport may experience repeated
takeoffs and landings. Crew members should be aware of this
risk.
3. The airport's complex taxiway system is prone to taxiing
errors. Crew members should be vigilant about this risk.
4. The airport's inadequate energy management may cause
excessive horizontal drift distance. Crew members should be
vigilant about this risk.
5. The airport's proximity to the ocean may create high risks at
the runway entrance. Crew members should be vigilant in
identifying these risks.
II. Core Threats
1. Airport Classification: Category I Complex Airport
(Operational Category)

Updated on 2025.10.20
Responsible Division: Second Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Due to the influence of coastal air currents, the grounding
attitude tends to be small.
2. The sea breeze is likely to cause a large low-level descent
rate and a steep slope.
II. Core Threats
1. Airport Classification: Category I Complex Airport (General
Category) (Refer to EFB Airport Characteristics Summary-Corporate
Complex Airport Classification and Operating Authority Rules)
2. Special complex procedures:

the PF controls landing), PAR, ASR (crew request)
(2) The 03L/03R runways have a special single-engine departure
procedure.
3. Command Characteristics:
(1) Both the VOR approach descent angle and PAPI lights are set
at 2.75°. Be mindful of visual discrepancies.
(2) Two runways, be sure to identify the landing runway.
(3) During the 21R RNP approach to the MAGRY point, the
subsequent profile is compact. Maintain timely deceleration and energy
management. It is strongly recommended to approach the MAGRY at an
altitude of 2000ft with a configuration of at least morph 2. Recent
incidents have occurred where aircraft have experienced go-around due
to inadequate energy management.
(4) The departure and approach procedures involve multiple altitude
window restrictions. During flight, the crew must comply with both the
maximum and minimum altitude limits.

Osaka Airport (KIX/RJBB)
Updated on 2026.6.8
Responsible Division: Second Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. A significant hard-landing event has previously occurred
during an RNAV approach.
2. Local airflow conditions may result in lower-than-normal
touchdown speeds.
3. Local airflow disturbances may increase the likelihood of
a bounced landing.
4. Tailwind conditions and inadequate energy management
have contributed to go-around events resulting from unstable
approaches.
5. Altitude Deviation / Unstable Approach Event: During
the ILS Z approach to Runway 24L, while descending through
approximately 1,200 ft on the published procedure, the crew
selected the missed-approach altitude after configuring the
aircraft for landing but before establishing the ILS glide path. As
a result, the aircraft failed to comply with published altitude
restrictions and did not intercept the glide path until
approximately 960 ft pressure altitude.
II. Core Threats
1. Command Characteristics:
(1) Prevent premature channel interception and avoid premature
standby for blind landing (to prevent the LOC assist function from
prematurely entering the channel). It is recommended to wait for the
APPR button in NAV mode only when the TO point on the ND is
AMBER (24L) and OTBON (06R).
非受控文件，仅供参考 FORREFERENCEONLY
547/1722
版本号 20260615
修改日期：2026 年 6 月 15 日
(2) High energy risk: The 06R often experiences favorable
winds and terrain effects, resulting in a compact descent profile.
Energy management is crucial.
(3) TCAS conflict risk: The approach and departure procedures
on Runway 24 overlap during operation. Select appropriate climb
mode to avoid unnecessary TCAS alerts, and recommend using a
smaller vertical speed (VS).
(4) After receiving clearance for ILS approach to RWY 24L, the
flight crew shall set a target altitude of 1200 FT on the FCU in
accordance with the aeronautical chart and perform managed
descent.
Meanwhile, the crew shall comply with the requirements specified in
the Flight Operations Technical Information Bulletin (Operational
Risk Alert for Low-Altitude Intermediate Approach Segments).
The crew shall pay attention to aircraft energy management and
avoid the aircraft entering a low-energy state.
2. Runway characteristics: Some sections of the airport runway
exhibit subsidence and gradient. After landing, it is recommended to
complete the single-engine procedure after passing the J3 or J4
uphill section, while maintaining control over taxiing speed to
prevent bumps and ensure smooth operation.
3. Other threats:

(1) When docking at spot8X departure, the standard procedure
is T-W6-Y. The system does not specify which gate or runway to
wait outside; the default is to wait at the runway end.
(2) When contacting the control tower, if no aircraft is in the
takeoff queue, the tower will issue a direct takeoff command. By
default, the aircraft enters the runway from the nose, and the crew
may request a cross-runway takeoff. In the absence of a takeoff
sequence, the tower will provide a direct takeoff command, allowing
the crew to autonomously select a non-full runway for takeoff.
(3) Osaka-Dalian: Radar-guided direct flight to GUMID, with

taxiing time is shorter. After preparation, the first contact with the
control tower should be to report READY.
(2) Adjust the MCDU single-shot speed-up altitude as required
based on fly smart calculations.
(3) For A321NEO aircraft taking off from a 06L/24R runway,
the VR (Vortex Rate) calculated using full runway data typically
exceeds 165 KT. The operating manual recommends TOGA
(Takeoff Off-Ground Approach) for takeoff. If performance permits,
the crew may use non-full runway calculations to reduce TOGA
usage, thereby saving engine maintenance costs while complying
with the manual's requirements.

(4) Entry:
1. Standard procedures: The 06R/24L Z procedure is typically
used for go-around, with the Y procedure occasionally employed.
For approach procedures, IGLEV & ATMUG B NAV (06R) and
IGLEV & ATMUG M (24L) are standard. In some cases, due to air

2. Command Characteristics:
(1) The landing runway employs two procedures: Y and Z. The
approach is typically radar-guided to IAF points BERRY or
MAYAH, followed by a blind landing clearance. For the 24L
runway, the command operates at 4,000 feet below 8,000 feet, with
MAYAH altitude maintained below 6,000 feet.
(2) For Runway 24L, ATC usually issues ILS instructions in
advance, and the VOR establishes a minimum ILS altitude of 1200 ft.
According to the latest policies, if the crew descends to 1200 ft, they
must maintain an attitude and intercept the ILS signal at a speed not
lower than 160 kt, or intercept the ILS normally at an altitude of
1600 ft. Pay attention to the timing of stabilization.
(3) Approach to IGLEV. Command FL180 to pass URDET,
then contact KANSAI APP (120.65) to enter IGLEV M. Maintain
FL180, then command 13,000 feet. During busy approaches, instruct
standard waiting at IGLEV and provide EFC time.
(4) Approach to the port in ATMUG direction, runway 24L.
Enter ATMUG M under ATC control, passing SAEKI at 170. Radar
guidance may be applied after MINOS. Proceed to runway 06R,
enter ATMUG B. Note: Fly MIBIB via BERRY. The track 059
directly faces runway 06L. Maintain situational awareness to avoid
misfocusing on the runway. Approach OTBON at 1600ft.

Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND/RJTT)
Updated on 2025.12.25
Responsibility Division: Division 5
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. The airport's multi-runway crossover operation poses a high
risk of runway incursion. Crew members should remain vigilant
to identify this hazard.
2. The airport's complex procedures may cause runway entrance
height illusions. Crew members should be vigilant about this
risk.
II. Core Threats
1. Airport Classification: Category I Complex Airports (General
Category) are detailed in the company's Complex Airport
Classification and Operating Procedures R6-1029.
2. Special complex procedures: EOSID, LDA, visual approach
3. Operational restrictions: RWY16L/R visual circling approach
is prohibited.
4. Command characteristics: The approach pattern is highly
complex and variable, requiring the crew to make all necessary
preparations in advance.
5. Runway characteristics: The airport lighting system is
complex, with some taxiways lacking centerline lights.
6. Other threats:
(1) For detailed analysis of complex procedures for entering and
exiting the airport, as well as the intricacies of taxiways, please
refer to the attached materials (Tokyo International Airport ATC
Office & Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and
Tourism Aviation Navigation Service Planning Department,
March 31,2024).
(2) Given the complex nighttime lighting conditions that
significantly impair runway detection, the LDA flight procedure
recommends constructing a reverse extension of the runway.
This approach not only enhances the crew's situational
awareness but also facilitates effective runway identification.

Fukuoka Airport (RJFF/FUK)
Updated on February 5, 2026
Responsibility Division: Fifth Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Due to the dim nighttime lighting at this airport, be cautious
of the risk of scraping the edge lights. The crew is advised to
remain vigilant about this hazard.
2. Due to the complex apron layout, this airport is prone to
taxiing errors. Crew members should be vigilant about this risk.
3. The airport's high-temperature effect may cause excessive
horizontal drift distance. Crew members should be alert to this
risk.
4. The airport's system design may cause runway entrance height
illusion. Crew members should be alert to this risk.
5. The airport's noise reduction procedure may cause aircraft to
approach below the glide path. Crew members should be alert to
this risk.
6. Due to crosswinds, the airport may experience steep runway
slopes. Crew members should be alert to this risk.
II. Core Threats
1. Airport Classification: Category I Complex Airports (General
Category) are detailed in the company's Complex Airport
Classification and Operating Procedures R6-1029.
2. Special Complex Procedures: 16L/R Runway EOSID
Program
3. Operational restrictions: The visual approach procedure is
prohibited.
4. Command Characteristics:
(1) May direct cross takeoffs from the E11 or E12 taxiways.
(Currently, FLYSMART only calculates takeoff performance for
full runways and E11)
(2) All approaching aircraft must notify Fukuoka control tower
of their intended landing runway upon initial contact, to prevent
runway misidentification (command characteristic).
(3) 34L/R runway, executing RNP/LOC
非受控文件，仅供参考 FORREFERENCEONLY

版本号 20260615
修改日期：2026 年 6 月 15 日
7. Pavement characteristics: The skid line is unclear, with no
skid lights, making it difficult to identify during rain or at night.
8. Terrain: The airport is located in a mountainous area with poor
clear air conditions. Special attention should be paid to
controlling MSA (Minimum Sustained Altitude) and the rate of
descent in low altitude.
9. Meteorological characteristics: Frequent tailwinds, high entry
elevation, long landing distance, and steep low-altitude slopes
often lead to over-limit incidents.

(2) When the tailwind component is within permissible limits,

(3) Fukuoka will commence operation of the new runway on

III. Operational Characteristics

3. Command Characteristics:

Communication Link) with ground frequency 121.925 to prevent
coordination issues. Release without repetition. Monitor ground
frequency 121.7 and prepare to report 'ready for push back' to the

(2) For clearance requests at altitudes other than those
specified in the flight plan, enter Pxxx (the requested
altitude level) in the PDC's remarks field.

opening and closing the fuel inlet, while the fuel gauge is
adjusted by the crew. The Fukuoka refueling personnel are
solely responsible for the refueling process. To avoid
complications, it is recommended to directly contact the
dispatcher for modifications to the release fuel quantity.

receiving the runway entry command, immediately halt entry and
verify instructions if the Runway Entrance Light (REL) is red; if
already on the runway, exit promptly and reconfirm.

Busan Airpor (PUS/RKPK)
Updated on 2025.12.01
Responsibility Division: Fifth Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. This airport is prone to terrain conflicts due to inherent flaws
in its historical approach procedures. Pilots are advised to remain
vigilant about this risk.
2. Due to similar runway markings, this airport may cause
misrunway incidents. Crew members should be vigilant about
this risk.
3. Due to turbulence, the airport experiences unstable approach
speeds, with a high risk of excessive approach speeds. The crew
is advised to be vigilant about this risk.
II. Core Threats
1. Airport Classification: Category II complex airport. Busan is a
special airport designated by the authority. For details, refer to
the company's classification of complex airports and operating
rules R6-1029.
2. Special complex procedure: visual circling
3. Operational restrictions: The company prohibits landing at
18L.
4. Runway characteristics: No taxiway between the two runways,
only a connecting runway. Keep a clear eye on the waiting line
and follow instructions carefully.
5. Terrain: The airport is surrounded by mountains on three sides
and is located close to them, resulting in complex terrain. The
36L/R departure and return runways have obstacles on one side,
requiring close turns.
6. Meteorological characteristics: The weather reports differ
significantly from the tower communications.
7. Military-civilian shared airport: During taxiing, the sunshade
must be lowered.
8. Other threats: Screen for other core threats.
(1) Move the 18R gate 600 meters inward and visually inspect
the runway to prevent mislanding.
(2) The aircraft must follow a predetermined taxiing route during
takeoff and landing (see Section 10-1P1-2.1 for details).
(3) The 18R aircraft may experience controllable ground collision
or unstable approach, requiring close monitoring of its position
and flight parameters.

Takarazuka Airport (TAK/RJOT)
Updated on 2025.12.10
Responsibility Division: Division 5
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Due to topographical constraints, this airport may have a steep
visual approach slope. Pilots should be alert to this risk.
2. Due to its coastal location, the airport may create a false sense
of elevation at the runway entrance. Crew members should be
vigilant about this risk.
I. Core Threats
1. Airport Classification: Category I Complex Airports (General
Category) are detailed in the company's Complex Airport
Classification and Operating Procedures R6-1029.
2. Special complex procedures: Visual approach (VA) and visual
circling approach (VCA) (VCA is prohibited at night)
3. Operational Restrictions: Visual approach and visual circling
approaches to Runway 08 at Takamatsu Airport are prohibited
unless the flight captain has obtained the company's authorization
for these procedures.
4. Command characteristics: Occasionally directs radar guidance
to conduct a blind landing 26 from the sea.
5. Terrain: The southwest, southeast, and south sides of the
airport feature elevated obstacles with relatively close clearance
distances, which may impair visual perception.

JIZHOU Airport (CJU/RKPC)
Updated on 4.7.2026
Responsible Division: Second Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Due to radar guidance and strong tailwinds, there was an
incident of go-around caused by an unstable approach.
2. Jeju is prone to low-level shear, which can lead to steep
low-level gradients and excessively long landing distances.
II. Core Threats
1. Airport classification: Category II complex airport
(maneuverable category). (Refer to EFB-
Airport Feature Summary-Company Complex Airport
Classification and Operating Authority Rules
2. Operational restrictions: The main runway 07/25 will be
closed from 14:00 to 20:00 Z (22:00-04:00 Beijing Time), except for
aircraft requesting 50 minutes in advance or emergency flights.
3. Command characteristics: Radar guidance with high energy;
Double interception risk at LIMSO point during the blind landing of
aircraft 07; Risk of approach speed exceeding limits.
4. Road surface characteristics: The ground has a short skid
distance, and the 3-minute limit should be observed.
5. Topography: Located near the coast, the southern side
features a dormant volcano standing over 6,000 feet tall.
6. Meteorological characteristics: During winter, runway
approach on 07 is characterized by strong headwinds, strong
crosswinds, and low-level wind shear.
7.Other threats:
(1) Characteristics of Korean communication pronunciation and
risks of communication impairment.
(2) Pursuant to Jeju NOTAM A 0098/26 ILS Z/Y RWY 07, the
decision height has been increased from 287 feet to 387 feet.

(5) On April 25, both ILS Z and LOC Z, as well as ILS Y and

I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. Frequent air traffic control instructions at this airport may
delay the establishment of landing patterns. Crew members
should be alert to this risk.
2. This airport is prone to morphing speed exceedance due
to procedural requirements and heavy workload. Crew members
should be vigilant in identifying this risk.
3. Due to airflow effects, this airport may cause excessive
horizontal drift distance. Crew members should be alert to this
risk.

restriction altitude in the go-around procedure.

5. Command Characteristics:
(1) For the 3000-meter five-point approach under general
command on the 19th, the procedure requires establishing
the five points. During radar-guided visual approach, the
radar-guided heading should generally maintain a
2700-meter five-point approach beyond the visual obstacle,
with attention to the five-point descent rate.
(2) During the approach phase in Lanzhou, the course must be
established using the second configuration with a speed of 170
knots or less.
(3) Upon XNN's arrival, the control center will first contact
the Xining approach. It may direct NODID to fly directly to
P15, specifying the approach method, runway, and approach
path. The control will then command a descent to the
standard pressure level of 5,400 meters early, as the
surrounding terrain is 14,000 feet high with limited obstacle
clearance. The crew should focus on controlling the descent
rate, opening the terrain, and maintaining a gentle descent.
Additionally, the approach terrain is highly bumpy, requiring
early precautions to avoid excessive low-altitude descent
rates that could trigger conflicts or terrain warnings.
(4) Unstable airflow increases the risk of exceeding speed
limits during takeoff and landing. All flight crews are
reminded to strictly follow SOPs and crew role assignments.
6. Pavement characteristics:
(1) Most inclined parking positions are prone to deviation

during approach. The approach sign displays a rapid

crossing the line.
7. Meteorological characteristics: Local turbulence and wind
shear are particularly prominent in spring and summer.
8.Other threats:
(1) Given the high-altitude airport and extended taxiway,
the crew must check brake temperature during cockpit
preparation to prevent overheating before takeoff, and
activate the brake fan if necessary.
(2) After the new runway became operational, Lanzhou
Airport updated its flight chart design. Pilots should pay
special attention to the changes in symbols and units in
the revised chart, such as the updated MSA 25NM
distance circle units and the introduction of 10NM
distance circles. For details, refer to Flight Department
Document No.078 [2025].
(3) Keep the flaps operation within 20,000 feet.
(4) Data analysis indicates this airport is prone to over speed
incidents. The crew must rigorously verify takeoff
performance metrics. The Pilot Manager (PM) should
promptly initiate wheel lifting at Vr speed, while the Flight
Controller (PF) must precisely regulate the lifting rate to
prevent over speed.

(5) To ensure a safe distance between the aircraft cabin door and
the boarding bridge floor after opening, safety boots are installed
within the accessible range for passengers and staff at the
movable end of the boarding bridge. Stepping on the safety
boots may reduce the height of the front end of the boarding
bridge, posing a risk of scraping against the aircraft. During the
operation of the boarding bridge, all individuals are prohibited
from stepping on the safety boots without valid reasons.
(6)
Due to increased bird activity, it is recommended that the
crew add a bird strike contingency plan to takeoff and approach
briefings.
(7)
2. To mitigate risks from rapid wind direction and speed
changes—such as triggering Alpha Floor protection or forced
landing—the crew should follow the "Energy Deficiency During
Landing Phase" guidelines. A decisive go-around is
recommended if any of the following occurs during landing: 1.
When the RA (Rate of Attitude) exceeds 100ft from the start of
the pull-up, and the indicated airspeed is below VLS (Virtually
Low Speed); 2. When the RA drops below 100ft, and the rate of
attitude increase is significantly mismatched with the rate of
descent (attitude increases but the descent rate fails to decrease
proportionally).
(8)
At high-altitude airports (elevation>1524 meters), takeoff
with engine components disabled is prohibited. If performance
calculations require disabled components, the APU bleed air
must be retained while enabling component takeoff. However, if
wing anti-icing is required during takeoff and initial climb, APU
非受控文件，仅供参考 FORREFERENCEONLY

修改日期：2026 年 6 月 15 日
bleed air must not be enabled for takeoff, and takeoff
performance must be calculated with components activated.
(9)
During prolonged taxiing under engine anti-icing conditions
or when ice shedding is required, frequent braking can cause
excessive brake temperatures. The ice shedding procedure further
accelerates temperature rise. However, brake fans at high-altitude
airports have limited cooling capacity. Since the ice shedding
procedure is typically synchronized with takeoff, this practice
may trigger post-takeoff brake overheating warnings.

incidents have shown that overbraking temperature warnings

4. Terrain: The airport area features flat terrain, with the

wind shear during approach, landing, and takeoff, which
significantly compromises flight safety.

19L (left departure) and 19R (right arrival). When flight

descent profile, maintain mental preparedness, and exercise
energy management. For frequency conversion approaches after

executing a Continuous Climb (CC) approach.

(6) Detailed description of typical unsafe incidents:
1. On April 19,2023, an A320 aircraft operating the
Yongzhou-Chongqing route was struck by a bird during its
approach phase at Chongqing Airport, where the radar dome was
hit at an altitude of 7,500 feet and an airspeed of 230 knots.
No impact on the control system, the aircraft continued to
approach for a normal landing. Post-landing inspection revealed
that the radar dome damage exceeded the tolerance limit,
measuring 278*175mm, and the radar dome was replaced.
On August 28,2023, an A320 aircraft was operating
a Chongqing-to-Xi 'an flight. During ground maintenance, the
pilot's headset was missing. Due to a misunderstanding, the aircraft
was mistakenly pushed forward. The right-seat pilot (PF) then
opened the side window to call maintenance for 'stop pushing,' by
which time the plane had already been pushed close to the taxiway
and towed back to its original position. Ground crews subsequently
provided a headset, established internal communication, and safely
pushed the aircraft forward for taxiing. The subsequent flight
proceeded normally.
3. On August 20,2023, during the final approach
phase of the B787 Chongqing flight, the system was triggered.
The sinkrate warning sounded, prompting the crew to execute a
go-around. After the decision to go around, the turbulence triggered
非受控文件，仅供参考 FORREFERENCEONLY
版本号 20260615
修改日期：2026 年 6 月 15 日
another sinkrate alert, and the crew proceeded with the go-around,
which went smoothly afterward.
4. On August 19,2025, the lead aircraft failed to
complete a straight-line departure from the runway in time due to
the preceding aircraft's request. The control tower instructed the
trailing aircraft to return to the runway, resulting in a 104-second
runway occupation by the lead aircraft.
5. On September 12,2025, the lead aircraft failed to complete a
right-angle departure from the runway in time due to the lead
aircraft's request. The control tower instructed the trailing aircraft to
return to the runway, resulting in a 94-second runway occupation by
the lead aircraft.

GUANGZHOU BAIYUN (ZGGG-CAN)
Updated on February 2, 2026
Responsibility Division: Seventh Division
I. Typical Safety Incidents
1. The airport has experienced incidents including bird strikes,
wind shear, and wrong takeoff events. Crew members are
advised to remain vigilant in identifying these risks.
II. Core Threats
1. Command Characteristics:
(1) The departure taxiway is marked as "YELLOW", and the
arrival taxiway is marked as "GREEN".
(2) In case of discrepancy between the flight plan's re-flight
altitude and the air traffic control command, the latter shall
prevail.
2. Pavement characteristics:
(1) The C temporary taxiway between L9 and L10 matches the
flight plan and requires a turn.
(2) After landing at 01L, the taxiway from E J23 to J14 features
a steep incline. We recommend performing a single-engine taxi
after this section.
3. Meteorological characteristics: From late spring to summer,
thunderstorms are frequent, with severe thunderstorms often
accompanied by low-level wind shear. During summer and
autumn, typhoons exert influence, bringing widespread strong
winds, heavy rainfall, and thunderstorms.
4. Other threats:
(1) The airport is highly busy with multiple adjacent airports,
requiring strict compliance with air traffic control directives to
prevent conflicts.
(2) Adjust the single-shot acceleration altitude according to the
fly Smart modification.
(3) The new procedure involves adjustments to multiple
programs and name changes, with height restrictions requiring
modifications. Please refer to the air chart for MCDU data
verification.

(3) During RNP08 approach, DG908 is in close proximity to IF and
